Standing at 6 ft 9.1 in (2.06 m) and weighing 201 lb (91 kg), Musa plays the [[small forward]] position. ==Early life== Musa was born in [[Bihać]], [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], as the second child of [[Bosniaks|Bosniak]] parents Rusmir and Saudina. He began playing [[association football]] at first, before choosing to focus on basketball. Musa started playing junior basketball in the youth setup at KK Bosna XXL, when he was 8 years old. He then moved to [[Sarajevo]]-based KK Koš, before joining Croatian team [[KK Cedevita]] in 2014. ==Professional career== In December 2014, he signed a deal with Croatian team [[KK Cedevita|Cedevita]].{{cite news|title=Cedevita Zagreb signs Dzanan Musa|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/croatia/145158/cedevita-zagreb-signs-bosnian-young-talent-dzanan-musa.html|accessdate=December 17, 2014|publisher=Sportando.com|date=December 17, 2014}} Musa made his debut in [[European professional club basketball system|Europe's top-tier]] level competition, the [[EuroLeague]], on 15 October 2015, making him [[List of youngest EuroLeague players since the 2000–01 season|the ninth-youngest player to make their debut in the EuroLeague since the 2000–01 season]] . Musa played the first 4:55 minutes of the game and recorded 4 points.{{cite news|title=Sixteen-year-old Musa makes historic Euroleague debut for Cedevita|url=http://www.fiba.com/news/sixteen-year-old-musa-makes-historic-euroleague-debut-for-cedevita|accessdate=May 19, 2016|publisher=FIBA.com|date=October 22, 2015}} In June 2017, Musa attended the Adidas Eurocamp, a basketball camp based in [[Treviso]] for international [[NBA draft]] prospects.{{Cite news|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/460604/dzanan-musa-headlines-adidas-eurocamp/|title=Dzanan Musa headlines the Adidas Eurocamp|date=7 June 2017|accessdate=12 April 2018|publisher=Eurohoops.net}} Musa was named the Eurocamp 2017 Most Improved Player.{{Cite news|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/dzanan-design|title=Dzanan Design|quote= He has already been praised for his improvement on D during 2017 Eurocamp (where he was chosen the most improved player) and showcased these skills during the tournament.|publisher=NBADraft.net|access-date=12 April 2018|date=9 July 2017}} In the [[2017–18 EuroCup Basketball|2017–18 season]], while a member of Cedevita, Musa was awarded the [[EuroCup Basketball Rising Star|EuroCup Rising Star Trophy]], after averaging 10.5 points and 3.2 rebounds per game, in 16 games played in Europe's 2nd-tier level [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] competition.{{Cite news|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/8n6qr9cnfdbmbm7m/7days-rising-star-trophy-winner-dzanan-musa-cedevita-zagreb.|title=2017-18 7DAYS EuroCup Rising Star Trophy winner: Džanan Musa, KK Cedevita|date=2 April 2018|accessdate=12 April 2018|publisher=EuroCup Basketball}} He was also named the [[ABA League Top Prospect]] as well as to the [[All-ABA League Team]] for the [[2017–18 ABA League First Division|2017–18 season]].{{cite web|url=http://www.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=40017|title=2017/18 Top Prospect: Džanan Musa (Cedevita)|publisher=www.aba-liga.com}}{{cite web|url=http://www.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=40039|title=Rochestie heads the Ideal Starting Five|publisher=www.aba-liga.com|access-date=12 April 2018}} On April 12, 2018, Musa declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]], where he is expected to be a first round selection.{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/usa/nba/271197/dzanan-musa-declares-for-the-2018-nba-draft.html|title=Dzanan Musa declares for the 2018 NBA Draft|date=12 April 2018|access-date=12 April 2018|publisher=Sportando.basketball}} He would be one of only 11 truly international underclassmen to remain in the NBA Draft that year. ==National team career== Musa played at the [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]] with the Bosnian national Under-16 team, leading the tournament in scoring, at 23.0 points per game. He also played at the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]], which he led in scoring, at 23.3 points per game, and in assisting, at 6.3 assists per game.[http://u16men.fibaeurope.com/en/default.asp] He also averaged 9.0 rebounds per game, during the tournament. In the tournament's finals game, against the tournament's hosts, [[Lithuania men's national under-16 and under-17 basketball team|Lithuania]], Musa scored 33 points, to go along with his 8 rebounds, 7 assists, 3 steals and 2 blocks, leading his team to an 85-83 victory, and securing a gold medal for his team.[http://u16men.fibaeurope.com/en/compID_YUjW-7-FJ,kK9s431Lyr41.season_2015.roundID_11538.gameID_11555-72-A-1.html] Musa was named the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship#Awards|MVP of the tournament]], and he was also selected to the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship#Awards|All-Tournament Team]]. Musa also played at the [[2016 FIBA Under-17 World Championship|2016 FIBA Under-17 World Cup]], which he led in scoring, at 34.0 points per game. He also averaged 8.1 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game. During the tournament, Musa scored 50 points, in 27 minutes played, in a game against Chinese Taipei, which is the current record for the most points scored in a single game at the [[FIBA Under-17
